# Embedded Systems Docs — Phase 1 Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Stand up the `docs/embedded/` section — all site wiring plus the first 51 pages (folders 00–04) — so a reader can go from "what is embedded" to a working bare-metal blink they understand line by line.

**Architecture:** A new top-level Docusaurus docs section with its own autogenerated sidebar and navbar tab, following the `docs/gpu-computing/` precedent. The one piece of real code is a build-time remark plugin that turns ` ```wavedrom ` fences into inline SVG via an MDX JSX component — no client-side JavaScript, no hydration. Content is plain Markdown using Mermaid, WaveDrom, `<Figure>`, `<Tabs>`, and admonitions.

**Tech Stack:** Docusaurus 3.10.2, React 19, Node 22, MDX v3, `wavedrom` + `onml` + `json5` (build-time SVG), `unist-util-visit`, `docusaurus-plugin-image-zoom`, Biome, Mermaid.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-embedded-systems-docs-design.md` — read it before starting. This plan implements Phase 1 of the three phases defined there. The spec's page-by-page outline is the source of truth for every page's title and content brief; this plan does not repeat those briefs.

## Global Constraints

Exact values, copied from the spec and from the verified repository baseline.

- **Section root:** `docs/embedded/`. Folders `00-overview` … `04-bare-metal-programming` in Phase 1.
- **Sidebar id:** `embeddedSidebar`. **Navbar label:** `Embedded Systems`. **Navbar icon:** `🔌`. Placed 7th, after GPU & Accelerators.
- **`_category_.json`:** 2-space indent, keys `label`, `position`, `link.type = "generated-index"`. `position` = numeric folder prefix + 1.
- **Frontmatter:** every topic page has `id`, `title`, `sidebar_label`, `sidebar_position`, `tags`. `tags` always starts with `embedded`. `sidebar_position` starts at 1 in each folder. `readme.md` omits `id`.
- **Page shape:** mental model before mechanism (never open with code, a register table, or a definition list) → optional `:::info[Prerequisites]` → body → **at least one visual anchor** → at least one `:::warning` naming a real day-costing mistake → `## See also` (3–5 relative links) → `## References` (2–6 annotated external sources, primary first; no bare URLs).
- **Admonitions:** only `:::info`, `:::note`, `:::tip`, `:::warning`. Do not invent others.
- **Code fences:** `c`, `cpp`, `rust`, `armasm`, `bash`, `cmake`, `make`/`makefile`, `ini`, `json`, `toml`, `diff`, `python`. Device tree, Kconfig, and linker scripts use ` ```text ` — there is no Prism grammar for them and ` ```c ` mis-highlights device tree.
- **WaveDrom:** at most 2–3 waveforms per page; ≤ 8 signals per waveform; every bit-field strip is paired with a semantics table giving field meaning and reset value.
- **Images:** `static/img/embedded/<folder-slug>/<name>.png`, referenced via `<Figure src="/img/embedded/..." />` with **no** `/knowledge-base` prefix. Every image needs a row in `static/img/embedded/SOURCES.md`. Source preference order: Bootlin (CC BY-SA) → Wikimedia Commons → vendor primary docs → own photographs. Never a blog or image-host copy.
- **Forward-link rule:** a Phase 1 page may link only to pages in folders 00–04 or to existing pages elsewhere in the repo. **Never link to folders 05–15** — they do not exist yet and `onBrokenLinks: "throw"` would fail the deploy. Name the future topic in prose without a link.
- **No-duplication contract:** the spec's normative table names existing pages that own their topics. Check it before drafting any page whose subject appears there; link, do not re-explain.
- **Commits:** per CLAUDE.md — `<type>: <what>` on one line, no body unless genuinely needed, **never** a `Co-Authored-By` trailer or a "Generated with Claude Code" line.

### Verified baseline (measured 2026-08-18, before any Phase 1 work)

- `npm run build` → **exit 0**. This is the correctness gate; `onBrokenLinks: "throw"` makes a broken internal link a build failure.
- `npm run typecheck` → **passes**. Keep it passing.
- `npm run lint` → **already fails with 157 errors and 28 warnings** across 225 pre-existing files (127 are formatting diffs). This is pre-existing debt unrelated to this work. **Do not gate tasks on repo-wide `npm run lint`, and do not "fix" unrelated files.** Gate on `npx biome check <the files this task touched>` being clean.

### Recommended model per task

The spec's dense-mechanism folders reward the stronger model; the descriptive ones do not.

| Tasks | Recommended model | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1–5 (infrastructure) | Opus 5 | Real code with a known MDX failure mode; every later diagram depends on it |
| 6 (00-overview), 7–8 (01-hardware-foundations) | Sonnet 5 acceptable | Descriptive; claims are checkable against vendor pages |
| 9–10 (02-processor-architecture), 13–14 (04-bare-metal-programming) | Opus 5 | Exact mechanism — register model, `EXC_RETURN`, lazy FPU stacking, `volatile` semantics — where fluent-but-wrong is the main risk |
| 11–12 (03-toolchain-and-build) | Opus 5 | Linker scripts and startup code; small errors produce advice that does not work |
| 15 (completion sweep) | Opus 5 | Cross-cutting consistency review |

## File Structure

**Created — infrastructure:**

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `src/plugins/remark-wavedrom.js` | The only real logic. Transforms ` ```wavedrom ` mdast code nodes into `mdxJsxFlowElement` nodes carrying pre-rendered SVG. Knows nothing about React or Docusaurus |
| `src/components/WaveDrom/index.js` | Presentation only. Wraps an SVG string in a `<figure>` on the existing light plate. Knows nothing about WaveDrom's format |
| `scripts/remark-wavedrom.test.mjs` | Unit tests for the plugin, run by Node's built-in test runner. Lives in `scripts/` (not `src/`) because `tsconfig.json` has `include: ["src"]` and `allowJs: true` |
| `static/img/embedded/SOURCES.md` | Image provenance manifest |

**Modified — infrastructure:**

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | 5 dependencies, 1 script |
| `sidebars.js` | `embeddedSidebar` entry |
| `docusaurus.config.js` | Navbar item, 4 Prism languages, `image-zoom` plugin, `remarkWavedrom` in docs `remarkPlugins` |
| `src/theme/MDXComponents.js` | Register `WaveDrom`, `Tabs`, `TabItem` globally so no page needs an import line |
| `src/css/custom.css` | `.kb-wavedrom` sizing and horizontal overflow |

**Created — content:** `docs/embedded/readme.md`, five `_category_.json` files, and 51 topic pages whose names and briefs are fixed by the spec's "Page-by-page outline" section.

The plugin/component split is deliberate: rendering WaveDrom source is a Node concern with heavyweight dependencies, and displaying an SVG is a React concern. Keeping them apart means the plugin is unit-testable without a DOM, which is what makes Task 2 a real TDD cycle.

### Task 2: The WaveDrom remark plugin

**Files:**
- Create: `src/plugins/remark-wavedrom.js`
- Create: `scripts/remark-wavedrom.test.mjs`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `wavedrom`, `onml`, `json5`, `unist-util-visit` from Task 1.
- Produces: a default-exported remark plugin factory `remarkWavedrom()`. It replaces each ` ```wavedrom ` code node with an `mdxJsxFlowElement` node named `WaveDrom` carrying attributes `svg` (string, the rendered SVG), `alt` (string, required), and optionally `caption` (string). Task 3's component consumes exactly these three props. Task 4 imports this module into `docusaurus.config.js`.

**Why this is tested when nothing else in the repo is:** the failure mode is silent and confusing. If the plugin ever emits a raw `html` node instead of a JSX node, MDX parses the `{` in WaveDrom's embedded `<style>` block as a JSX expression and the build dies with an error that points at the Markdown file, not at the plugin. Test 3 below is the regression guard for exactly that.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

Create `scripts/remark-wavedrom.test.mjs`:

```js
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import remarkWavedrom from "../src/plugins/remark-wavedrom.js";

// Runs the transformer over a one-node tree and returns the transformed node.
// `file.fail` is how remark reports a fatal error; we make it throw so tests can catch it.
function transform(node) {
  const tree = { type: "root", children: [node] };
  const file = {
    fail(message) {
      throw new Error(message);
    },
  };
  remarkWavedrom()(tree, file);
  return tree.children[0];
}

function fence(value, meta) {
  return { type: "code", lang: "wavedrom", meta, value };
}

const WAVE = "{ signal: [{name: 'clk', wave: 'p...'}] }";
const REG = "{ reg: [{bits: 2, name: 'MODE'}, {bits: 30, name: 'rest'}] }";

test("renders a signal fence to an mdxJsxFlowElement", () => {
  const out = transform(fence(WAVE, 'alt="clock"'));
  assert.equal(out.type, "mdxJsxFlowElement");
  assert.equal(out.name, "WaveDrom");
  const svg = out.attributes.find((a) => a.name === "svg");
  assert.ok(svg.value.startsWith("<svg"));
  assert.ok(svg.value.includes("</svg>"));
});

test("renders a reg fence to a bit-field diagram", () => {
  const out = transform(fence(REG, 'alt="MODE field"'));
  const svg = out.attributes.find((a) => a.name === "svg");
  assert.ok(svg.value.startsWith("<svg"));
  assert.ok(svg.value.includes("MODE"));
});

// The regression guard. A raw `html` node would make MDX parse WaveDrom's
// embedded <style> block as JSX and fail the build.
test("never emits a raw html node", () => {
  const out = transform(fence(WAVE, 'alt="clock"'));
  assert.notEqual(out.type, "html");
});

test("passes title through as a caption and alt as alt", () => {
  const out = transform(fence(WAVE, 'title="SPI mode 0" alt="SPI mode 0 timing"'));
  const attr = (n) => out.attributes.find((a) => a.name === n)?.value;
  assert.equal(attr("caption"), "SPI mode 0");
  assert.equal(attr("alt"), "SPI mode 0 timing");
});

test("falls back to title when alt is absent", () => {
  const out = transform(fence(WAVE, 'title="SPI mode 0"'));
  const attr = (n) => out.attributes.find((a) => a.name === n)?.value;
  assert.equal(attr("alt"), "SPI mode 0");
});

test("fails the build when neither alt nor title is given", () => {
  assert.throws(() => transform(fence(WAVE, undefined)), /alt=|title=/);
});

test("fails the build on unparseable source", () => {
  assert.throws(() => transform(fence("{ signal: [", 'alt="x"')), /JSON5|parse/i);
});

test("leaves other code fences untouched", () => {
  const node = { type: "code", lang: "c", value: "int main(void) { return 0; }" };
  const out = transform(node);
  assert.equal(out.type, "code");
  assert.equal(out.lang, "c");
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the plugin**

Create `src/plugins/remark-wavedrom.js`:

```js
import JSON5 from "json5";
import onml from "onml";
import { visit } from "unist-util-visit";
import wavedrom from "wavedrom";

// Build-time WaveDrom rendering. Turns ```wavedrom fences into pre-rendered
// SVG carried by the <WaveDrom /> MDX component (src/components/WaveDrom).
//
// The node MUST be an mdxJsxFlowElement, never a raw `html` node: WaveDrom's
// skin embeds a <style> block containing CSS braces, which MDX v3 would parse
// as a JSX expression and fail the build on.
//
// Fence meta: ```wavedrom title="SPI mode 0" alt="SPI mode 0 timing"

const META_PAIR = /(\w+)="([^"]*)"/g;

function parseMeta(meta) {
  const parsed = {};
  if (!meta) return parsed;
  for (const [, key, value] of meta.matchAll(META_PAIR)) {
    parsed[key] = value;
  }
  return parsed;
}

export default function remarkWavedrom() {
  return (tree, file) => {
    // renderAny uses this to namespace generated element ids; it only has to be
    // unique within one page, and the transformer runs once per file.
    let diagramIndex = 0;

    visit(tree, "code", (node, index, parent) => {
      if (node.lang !== "wavedrom" || !parent) return;

      const { title, alt } = parseMeta(node.meta);
      const label = alt || title;
      if (!label) {
        file.fail(
          'wavedrom fence needs alt="..." (or title="..." to fall back to)',
          node,
        );
      }

      let source;
      try {
        source = JSON5.parse(node.value);
      } catch (error) {
        file.fail(`wavedrom fence is not valid JSON5: ${error.message}`, node);
      }

      const svg = onml.stringify(
        wavedrom.renderAny(diagramIndex, source, wavedrom.waveSkin),
      );
      diagramIndex += 1;

      const attributes = [
        { type: "mdxJsxAttribute", name: "svg", value: svg },
        { type: "mdxJsxAttribute", name: "alt", value: label },
      ];
      if (title) {
        attributes.push({
          type: "mdxJsxAttribute",
          name: "caption",
          value: title,
        });
      }

      parent.children[index] = {
        type: "mdxJsxFlowElement",
        name: "WaveDrom",
        attributes,
        children: [],
      };
    });
  };
}
```

### Task 3: The WaveDrom component and global MDX components

**Files:**
- Create: `src/components/WaveDrom/index.js`
- Modify: `src/theme/MDXComponents.js`
- Modify: `src/css/custom.css` (append after the `.kb-figure__credit a` rule, currently ending near line 1104)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the `svg`, `alt`, and `caption` props produced by Task 2's plugin.
- Produces: `WaveDrom`, `Tabs`, and `TabItem` available in every `.md` page in `docs/` with no import line. Task 5 and every later content task rely on this.

Registering `Tabs`/`TabItem` globally is what lets all 174 pages stay plain `.md` — the spec chose this over a mixed `.md`/`.mdx` tree.

- [ ] **Step 1: Create the component**

Create `src/components/WaveDrom/index.js`:

```jsx
// <WaveDrom /> — a WaveDrom timing waveform or register bit-field strip,
// rendered to SVG at build time by src/plugins/remark-wavedrom.js. Nothing
// renders on the client; this component only places the finished SVG.
//
// WaveDrom's default skin draws black strokes on a transparent canvas, so the
// diagram sits on the same permanent light plate <Figure /> uses for
// third-party technical diagrams. See src/components/Figure/index.js.
//
// Authored in markdown as:
//   ```wavedrom title="SPI mode 0" alt="SPI mode 0 timing"
//   { signal: [ ... ] }
//   ```
export default function WaveDrom({ svg, alt, caption }) {
	return (
		<figure className="kb-figure kb-wavedrom">
			<div
				className="kb-figure__plate"
				role="img"
				aria-label={alt}
				// biome-ignore lint/security/noDangerouslySetInnerHtml: trusted, build-time WaveDrom output
				dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: svg }}
			/>
			{caption && (
				<figcaption className="kb-figure__caption">{caption}</figcaption>
			)}
		</figure>
	);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Register it globally**

In `src/theme/MDXComponents.js`, add the imports below the existing `Figure` import:

```js
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";
import WaveDrom from "@site/src/components/WaveDrom";
```

:::warning[The `@theme` alias in this repo is not what it looks like]
`src/plugins/webpack-alias.js` aliases `@theme` to `src/theme/`, which contains no `Tabs`.
`@theme/Tabs` still resolves to the classic theme's component because Docusaurus registers a
longer, more specific `@theme/Tabs` alias and webpack prefers the longest matching prefix. Use
`@theme/Tabs` — **not** `@theme-original/Tabs`, which is only valid inside a swizzled component of
that same name, and not a relative path into `node_modules`. Task 5 proves the resolution works in
a real build; if it ever fails there, the fallback is
`import Tabs from "@docusaurus/theme-classic/lib/theme/Tabs";`.
:::

and extend the default export:

```js
export default {
	...MDXComponents,
	Icon,
	Figure,
	WaveDrom,
	Tabs,
	TabItem,
};
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the stylesheet rules**

Append to `src/css/custom.css`:

```css
/* WaveDrom diagrams (src/components/WaveDrom) sit on the same light plate as
   <Figure />. WaveDrom emits SVGs with explicit pixel widths (a 32-bit register
   strip is 800px, wider than the content column), so wide diagrams scroll
   inside the figure rather than being scaled down into illegibility, and the
   page body never scrolls horizontally. */
.kb-wavedrom .kb-figure__plate {
  overflow-x: auto;
  /* The plate centers with justify-content, but centering an overflowing
     scroll container makes its leading edge unreachable; the auto margin
     below centers narrow diagrams without that failure mode. */
  justify-content: flex-start;
}

.kb-wavedrom svg {
  display: block;
  /* The plate is a flex container: without this the SVG is shrunk to fit
     instead of overflowing, which is the bug this block exists to avoid. */
  flex-shrink: 0;
  /* Centers when the diagram fits; resolves to 0 when it overflows. */
  margin-inline: auto;
}
```

:::warning[Do not reintroduce `max-width: 100%` here]
An earlier revision of this plan specified `max-width: 100%; height: auto;` on `.kb-wavedrom svg`.
That is wrong and was caught in Task 3's review. WaveDrom SVGs carry explicit pixel `width`/`height`
plus a `viewBox`, so `max-width: 100%` scales them *down* to fit and the plate's `overflow-x: auto`
never triggers — wide diagrams squash instead of scrolling. `.kb-figure__plate` is also a flex
container (`@apply flex w-full justify-center …`), so `flex-shrink: 0` is required as well or the
flex parent squashes the SVG by a second, independent mechanism.
:::

### Task 5: Prove the rendering pipeline end to end

**Files:**
- Create then delete: `docs/embedded/pipeline-smoke-test.md`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: everything from Tasks 1–4.
- Produces: verified evidence that ` ```wavedrom ` fences, `<Tabs>`, `<Figure>`, and image zoom all work in a production build. No lasting artifact.

## Hardware target (assumption — change here, once)

The spec deliberately left the board unnamed. This plan pins it, because every register example
in folders 02–04 inherits the choice:

| Item | Choice |
|---|---|
| Board | **NUCLEO-F411RE** |
| MCU | STM32F411RE — Arm Cortex-M4F, 100 MHz, 512 KB flash, 128 KB SRAM |
| Board user manual | ST **UM1724**, *STM32 Nucleo-64 boards* |
| MCU reference manual | ST **RM0383**, *STM32F411xC/E advanced Arm-based 32-bit MCUs* |
| Core programming manual | ST **PM0214**, *STM32 Cortex-M4 MCUs and MPUs programming manual* |
| Architecture reference | Arm *Armv7-M Architecture Reference Manual* |
| Toolchain | Arm GNU Toolchain (`arm-none-eabi-gcc`) + CMake + OpenOCD |

Chosen because it is cheap, stocked everywhere, has an on-board ST-LINK (no separate probe to
buy), and has a Cortex-M4F — so the FPU, MPU, and DSP pages in folder 02 have real hardware behind
them rather than being hypothetical.

**To override:** change this table and the page-level citations in Tasks 9–14. Nothing structural
depends on the part.

## Content task recipe

Tasks 6–14 all write Markdown. They share this procedure; each task then names its own folder,
pages, visual anchors, and primary sources.

There is no TDD cycle for prose. The equivalent feedback loop is: **write the page → build →
check it against the conventions → commit.** The build is not a formality: `onBrokenLinks:
"throw"` turns a mistyped relative link into a deploy failure.

For each page:

1. Read that page's row in the spec's "Page-by-page outline" — that brief is the requirement.
2. Check the spec's no-duplication table. If an existing page owns the topic, link to it with a
   correct relative path (e.g. `../../computer-science/buses-and-io/io-and-interrupts.md`) and
   write only what is *additional*.
3. Write the page to the shape in Global Constraints: mental model first, visual anchor, a real
   `:::warning`, `## See also`, `## References`.
4. Every concrete number (a latency, a register reset value, a current draw) cites the document
   and section it came from.

Then, once per task:

5. Run `npm run build`. Expected: exit 0.
6. Run the conventions check below. Fix anything it flags.
7. Commit with `docs: add <folder label> pages`.

**Conventions check** — run from the repo root, substituting the folder:

```bash
FOLDER=docs/embedded/00-overview
# every page has the five required frontmatter keys
for f in $FOLDER/*.md; do
  for k in id title sidebar_label sidebar_position tags; do
    grep -q "^$k:" "$f" || echo "MISSING $k: $f"
  done
done
# every page ends with the two required sections
grep -L "^## See also" $FOLDER/*.md
grep -L "^## References" $FOLDER/*.md
# every page has a visual anchor (mermaid, wavedrom, Figure, or a table)
for f in $FOLDER/*.md; do
  grep -qE '^```(mermaid|wavedrom)|<Figure|^\|' "$f" || echo "NO VISUAL ANCHOR: $f"
done
# every page names a real mistake
grep -L ":::warning" $FOLDER/*.md
# no forward links into folders that do not exist yet
grep -rnE '\((\.\./)*0[5-9]-|\((\.\./)*1[0-5]-' $FOLDER/*.md && echo "FORWARD LINK FOUND"
```

The last check is the one that protects the deploy. It must print nothing.

**before** the clock frequency, or the part locks up.

because it is the correct answer to the race the `volatile` page raises.

Each gets its own plan document, written from the same spec, when the previous phase is merged.
Neither is expanded here — writing task detail for pages 52–174 now would go stale against what
Phase 1 teaches us.

| Phase | Folders | Pages | Plan file |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 — The working engineer | 05 Peripherals, 06 Real-time, 07 RTOS, 09 Low power, 11 Debugging | 55 | `<date-written>-embedded-phase-2.md` |
| 3 — Systems and shipping | 08 Connectivity, 10 Linux, 12 Safety, 13 Security, 14 Lifecycle, 15 Languages | 68 | `<date-written>-embedded-phase-3.md` |

Plan filenames follow the repository convention `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>.md`,
dated the day the plan is written.

**Carried into both:** the forward-link rule (a page may only link to its own phase or earlier),
the per-file lint gate, the conventions check script from this plan, and the `SOURCES.md`
discipline. **Phase 2's first task** should add backlinks from Phase 1 pages to the folder 11
debugging material that Phase 1 could only mention in prose.
